s2.ptxt: When replacing with a new compressor assembly (with pulley), gradually release the inert (helium) gas from the service valve, then drain the amount of oil shown below before installation.

specitem.ptxt: Oil capacity 30mL (amount to drain when replacing)

item.ptxt: Since compressor oil remains in the vehicle piping, if a new compressor assembly (with pulley) is installed without draining its oil, the amount of oil will become excessive, interfering with heat exchange in the refrigerant cycle and causing poor cooling or adverse effects such as noise and vibration.

s2.ptxt: Remove the suction seal cap.
Drain the oil while lightly shaking the compressor with the suction port facing down. (*1)

atten3.ptxt: Be careful not to get compressor oil on the pulley.

s2.ptxt: With the DL pulley side facing down, rotate the pulley clockwise 10 times at a speed of about 1 time every 2 seconds. (*2)

atten3.ptxt: Gas or oil may spray out when the pulley is rotated, so be careful not to bring your face close to the compressor ports.

s2.ptxt: Quickly turn the DL pulley side upward and rotate the pulley clockwise 1 times. (*3)
Perform the operation (*1) above to drain the oil. (*4)
Repeat the operations (*2) to (*4) above about 5 times to drain the standard amount of oil.
Using a Torx socket wrench (E8), temporarily install the compressor assembly (with pulley) with 2 stud bolts.
Install the compressor assembly (with pulley) with 2 bolts and 2 nuts in the order shown in the illustration.
Connect the connector.
Peel off the vinyl tape wrapped around the joints of the discharge hose and compressor assembly (with pulley).
Apply sufficient compressor oil (ND-OIL8) to a new O-ring and the fitting surface of the compressor assembly (with pulley).
Install the O-ring to the discharge hose.

atten3.ptxt: Do not allow dirt or foreign matter to adhere to the O-ring or O-ring sealing surface.

s2.ptxt: Install the discharge hose to the compressor assembly (with pulley) with the bolt.
Peel off the vinyl tape wrapped around the joints of the suction hose and compressor assembly (with pulley).
Apply sufficient compressor oil (ND-OIL8) to a new O-ring and the fitting surface of the compressor assembly (with pulley).
Install the O-ring to the suction hose.

atten3.ptxt: Do not allow dirt or foreign matter to adhere to the O-ring or O-ring sealing surface.

s2.ptxt: Install the suction hose to the compressor assembly (with pulley) with the bolt.
Evacuate the system using a vacuum pump.
Charge with refrigerant HFC-134a (R134a).

atten3.ptxt: Never operate the cooler compressor before charging refrigerant, as operating it without refrigerant may cause it to seize due to insufficient lubrication.

atten4.ptxt: When reusing recovered refrigerant gas, the recovery rate of the refrigerant recovery/recycling machine is approximately 90%, so additional refrigerant from a service can is required when recharging; prepare it in advance.

When reusing the belt, inspect the entire circumference of the ribs and back for wear and cracks, and replace it if wear or cracks reach the core (1 or more places) or if the rib rubber is chipped (1 or more places).

s2.ptxt: Using SST, slowly turn the V-belt tensioner clockwise and install the V-belt.

item.ptxt: Check that the SST and tools are securely set.
When compressing the V-belt tensioner, slowly apply force perpendicular to the tool, taking 3 seconds or more.

s2.ptxt: Check that the belt is fitted on each pulley.
Check that the belt is correctly set on each pulley.
Start the engine and check that the belt rotates smoothly with no abnormal noise.

atten3.ptxt: After charging with refrigerant, perform a break-in operation at 2000r/min or less for 2 minutes or more.

s2.ptxt: After charging the refrigerant gas, inspect for refrigerant gas leaks using a halogen leak detector.
Install the radiator upper air deflector with the 8 clips.

s-1.ptxt: Install Engine Under Cover Rear RH

atten4.ptxt: Use the same procedure for the RH side as for the LH side.
